newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins edge up after fall on freeze fears.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins edge up after fall on freeze fears.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds recovered some ground in thin trading after an early nervous fall on fears further bonds could have been frozen, dealers said on Tuesday.
No comment from officials in the Finance Ministry or Vneshtorgbank, the main MinFin depositary, was available on Tuesday.
Dealers said on Monday that prices were falling amid rumours that some banks had been advised that some of their MinFins, totalling more than $50 million face value, had been frozen.

A Russian police officer working on a frozen MinFin case told Reuters on Monday that a large volume of Russian MinFin bonds may have been frozen this May in addition to the $24 million previously reported.
"Many banks have stepped aside until the whole problem is resolved. Trading has become much less liquid," one dealer said.
But dealers said prices firmed in late thin trading by around 0.5 point.
"A small amount of buying would be enough to push up prices," Most Bank dealer Alexander Rodionov said.
Dealers said price fluctuations in the nearest days will entirely depend on further news about frozen MinFins.
